extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of sociology, social theory, and economic history
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative principles and causal criteria used to explain class-differentiated religious and non-religious behaviours in advanced industrial societies (Veblen's analysis of the leisure class). Useful for sociological critique or historical analysis of class, religion, and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation of low economic efficiency/intelligence with devoutness
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule the classes that are low in economic efficiency, or in intelligence, or both, are peculiarly devout--as, for instance, the Negro population of the South, much of the lower-class foreign population, much of the rural population, especially in those sections which are backward in education...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: Southern Negroes, lower-class foreign elements, rural backward areas. Explanation: these groups retain animistic or anthropomorphic religious habits because their everyday life is remote from modern industrial processes and educational development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artisan class secularization from industrial exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: The artisan class, on the other hand, is notoriously falling away from the accredited anthropomorphic creeds and from all devout observances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: artisans are exposed to organized industry requiring 'recognition of the undisguised phenomena of impersonal, matter-of-fact sequence' and conformity to cause-and-effect, which undermines animistic/anthropomorphic thinking and produces undevout skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle-class nominal support but declining male devotional fervor
rubrics_metrics.description: The case of the lower or doubtful leisure class in America--the middle class commonly so called--... The churches still have the pecuniary support of this class; although the creeds to which the class adheres with the greatest facility are relatively poor in anthropomorphic content. At the same time the effective middle-class congregation tends... to become a congregation of women and minors. There is an appreciable lack of devotional fervor among the adult males of the middle class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator: financial/supportive backing of institutions persists even as substantive belief or male participation declines; congregational demographics (women and children) signal this shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women’s vicarious leisure leads to stronger devoutness
rubrics_metrics.description: This peculiar sexual differentiation... is due, at least in part, to the fact that the middle-class women are in great measure a (vicarious) leisure class. ... the women of civilized communities owe, in great measure, to their economic position. ... The logic, and the logical processes, of her everyday domestic life are carried over into the realm of the supernatural, and the woman finds herself at home and content in a range of ideas which to the man are in great measure alien and imbecile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: economic/dependent domestic position and patriarchal status conserve archaic habits of thought; domestic reasoning transposes to religious belief, explaining greater female religiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patriarchal relations conserve archaic devotion in upper middle class
rubrics_metrics.description: The men of the upper middle class commonly take a more complacent attitude towards devout observances than the men of the artisan class. ... the patriarchal relation of status which still persists in their conjugal life and in their habitual use of servants, may also act to conserve an archaic habit of mind and may exercise a retarding influence upon the process of secularization...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signs: sheltered life, household servants, and persisting status relations correlate with retained religious forms even when industrial contact is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Southern devoutness linked to lower industrial development and archaic practices
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no hereditary leisure class of any consequence in the American community, except in the South. This Southern leisure class is somewhat given to devout observances; more so than any class of corresponding pecuniary standing in other parts of the country. It is also well known that the creeds of the South are of a more old-fashioned cast than their counterparts in the North. Corresponding to this more archaic devotional life of the South is the lower industrial development of that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary evidence: prevalence of archaic offenses (duels, brawls, feuds, gambling) and a 'livelier sense of honor' suggest a closer fit to predatory/archaic culture that supports devoutness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper-class ritualism as reversion to primitive spectacle
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a tendency perceptible among the upper-class worshippers to affiliate themselves with those cults which lay relatively great stress on ceremonial and on the spectacular accessories of worship... a tendency to return to this naive, sensational method of appeal is unmistakable in the upper-class churches of today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators include: colored lights, orchestral music, incense, processionals, genuflexions, and spectacle; interpreted as a primitive/archaic mode of appeal linked to wealth and leisure rather than doctrinal fervor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial/mechanical employments promote undevout skepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The habitual activity of the men engaged in these branches of industry has greatly changed ... the discipline to which the mechanician is exposed in his daily employment affects the methods and standards of his thinking also on topics which lie outside his everyday work. ... the grounds of generalization habitually present ... is an enforced cognizance of matter-of-fact sequence. The result ... is a proclivity to undevout scepticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criterion: degree of contact with impersonal, organized industrial processes predicts loss of animistic/anthropomorphic interpretation and decline in devout observance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devout habit aligns with predatory/personal-status cultures, not industrial life
rubrics_metrics.description: The devout habit of mind attains its best development under a relatively archaic culture... It appears also that this devout attitude marks a type of human nature which is more in consonance with the predatory mode of life than with the later-developed, more consistently and organically industrial life process of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as analytical lens: if culture emphasizes mastery/subservience and personal status, expect stronger devout observances; if culture emphasizes impersonal industrial processes, expect weakening of devoutness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leisure class conserves and rehabilitates archaic cultural traits
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution of a leisure class acts to conserve, and even to rehabilitate, that archaic type of human nature and those elements of the archaic culture which the industrial evolution of society in its later stages acts to eliminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: presence of a leisure class predicts survival of traits (ritualism, predatory aptitudes) otherwise eliminated by industrial adaptation; evaluate degree of sheltering and reputability sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-invidious motives (charity, sociability, aesthetic congruity) sustain religious forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Among these alien motives which affect the devout scheme... may be mentioned the motives of charity and of social good-fellowship, or conviviality; ... A still more characteristic and more pervasive alien element ... is that non-reverent sense of aesthetic congruity with the environment, which is left as a residue of the latter-day act of worship after elimination of its anthropomorphic content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These motives blend with devout forms to maintain ecclesiastical institutions in name/form even among those who abandon anthropomorphic belief; evaluate organizations for the mix of aesthetic/solidarity vs. doctrinal motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-invidious impulses oppose leisure-class canons of waste and invidious comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: This non-invidious residue of the religious life... as well as the impulse of charity or of sociability, act in a pervasive way to shape men's habits of thought for the economic purpose. ... The basis of that institution... is the habit of invidious comparison; and this habit is incongruous with the exercise of the aptitudes now in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical test: when non-invidious impulses (solidarity, efficiency, charity) grow, they undermine leisure-class values of waste and invidious emulation; measure tension between these sets of motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leisure-class activities often mixed-motive with reduced economic efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: In all this latter-day range of leisure-class activities that proceed on the basis of a non-invidious and non-religious interest, it is to be noted that the women participate more actively and more persistently than the men... Where this devout coloring is present it lowers the immediate efficiency of the organizations for any economic end to which their efforts may be directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: charitable organizations split attention between devotional and secular aims; evaluate such groups for extent of devotional influence reducing practical economic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ostensible ameliorative works often motivated by invidious self-regard
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a matter of sufficient notoriety ... that extraneous motives are commonly present among the incentives to this class of work--motives of a self-regarding kind, and especially the motive of an invidious distinction. ... many ostensible works of disinterested public spirit are no doubt initiated and carried on with a view primarily to the enhance repute or even to the pecuniary gain, of their promoters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator: conspicuous expenditure (foundations, libraries, museums) and publicized philanthropy suggest reputability motives; adjust evaluation of social value to discount invidious incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement/mission-of-culture approach substitutes wasteful upper-class proprieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the efforts now in reputable vogue for the amelioration of the indigent population of large cities are of the nature, in great part, of a mission of culture. ... They are commonly persons of an exemplary life and gifted with a tenacious insistence on ceremonial cleanness ... The cultural or civilizing efficacy of this inculcation of correct habits of thought ... is scarcely to be overrated; nor is its economic value to the individual who acquires these higher and more reputable ideals inconsiderable. ... the effect wrought is in large part a substitution of costlier or less efficient methods of accomplishing the same material results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating settlement-type interventions, check for whether reform emphasizes upper-class manners/consumption (punctilios) that may raise reputability but substitute less efficient means for achieving material improvement.
